import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 851

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/851](https://www.erdosproblems.com/851)
- [Pr26] D. Price and GPT-5.2 Pro, [Erdős problem 851](https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e) (2026)
-/

namespace Erdos851

/--
`TwoPowAddSet r` is the set of integers of the form `2^k+n`, where `k ≥ 0` and `n` has at most `r`
prime divisors.
-/
def TwoPowAddSet (r : ℕ) := {(2 ^ k + n) | (k : ℕ) (n : ℕ) (_ : n.primeFactors.card ≤ r)}

/-- The set of integers of the form `2^k+p`, where `k ≥ 0` and `p` is prime. -/
def twoPowAddPrimeSet : Set ℕ := {(2 ^ k + p) | (k : ℕ) (p : ℕ) (_ : p.Prime)}

/--
The set of integers of the form `2^k+p` (where `p` is prime) has positive lower density.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_851.variants.romanoff : 0 < Set.lowerDensity twoPowAddPrimeSet := by
  sorry

/--
Let $\epsilon > 0$. Is there some $r \ll_\epsilon 1$ such that the density of integers of the
form $2^k+n$, where $k \geq 0$ and $n$ has at most $r$ prime divisors, is at least $1-\epsilon$?

This was proved affirmatively by Price and GPT-5.2 Pro [Pr26].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_851 (ε : ℝ) (hε : ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) : ∃ r d,
    (TwoPowAddSet r).HasDensity d ∧ 1 - ε ≤ d := by
  sorry

end Erdos851

findings.description: The conclusion `∃ r d, (TwoPowAddSet r).HasDensity d ∧ 1 - ε ≤ d` requires the natural-density limit to exist. The problem asks only for a lower-density bound. `Set.HasDensity` unfolds to `Filter.Tendsto`, whereas lower density is a `liminf`; requiring convergence adds a condition absent from both the original problem and the cited solution. Although the website's abbreviated statement says merely “density,” the primary sources explicitly specify lower density.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, [Er85c], “On some of my problems in number theory I would most like to see solved,” p. 75, explicitly asks about the “lower density” of these integers: https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-17.pdf. The cited Price/GPT manuscript, Theorem 1, states `liminf_{x→∞} #(A_r ∩ [1,x])/x ≥ 1−ε`; Remark 1 gives the same conclusion for distinct prime factors: https://www.overleaf.com/read/svgbjzpxxppv#4eea7e.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the conclusion with `∃ r : ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity`, and specify “lower density” in the theorem docstring. The existing restriction `ε ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1` can remain.

findings.description: The bibliography entry `[Pr26]` at line 24 credits “D. Price.” The cited contribution is by Liam Price, so the author's initial is incorrect.
findings.source_evidence: The source page thanks Liam Price, and the comment introducing the linked Overleaf manuscript is signed “Liam Price,” dated 5 February 2026: https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/851.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “D. Price” to “L. Price” or “Liam Price” in the `[Pr26]` reference.

reformulations.difference: Considering the ε-domain separately from the density defect, Lean quantifies only over `0 < ε < 1`, rather than every `ε > 0`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Restriction gives one direction. Conversely, for ε ≥ 1, reuse the witnesses for ε = 1/2: their density bound d ≥ 1/2 implies d ≥ 1−ε. The exact equivalence between these two ε-domains for the existing existential `HasDensity` conclusion was proved in scratch Lean.

reformulations.difference: The supporting definition permits `n = 0`, because `Nat.primeFactors 0 = ∅`, whereas the manuscript requires `n ≥ 1`. This is harmless for the density assertions, independently of the reported limit-existence defect.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let A_r be the version requiring n > 0 and S_r be `TwoPowAddSet r`. Scratch Lean proves A_r ⊆ S_r and S_r \ A_r ⊆ {2^k : k ∈ ℕ}. Therefore their counting functions below N differ by at most O(log N), and their partial densities differ by a quantity tending to zero. They have identical lower densities and, for every d, S_r.HasDensity d iff A_r.HasDensity d. The set inclusions were formalized; the density equivalence itself was not.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. The Romanoff variant matches the sources. `primeFactors.card` correctly counts distinct prime divisors: this agrees with Erdős's definition of ω and the manuscript's Remark 1, so there is no multiplicity defect. Both solved tags agree with the source's recorded status. The original strict lower bound versus a non-strict bound is harmless after shrinking ε; this generic equivalence was also checked in Lean. Boundary computations and auxiliary proofs compile without errors or warnings in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/density-check.lean. Erdős pages were read through a text proxy after direct requests encountered browser challenges; the Overleaf LaTeX source was downloaded through its public read-only link. No repository files were edited.

submission.summary: Replaced the natural-density existence requirement with `∃ r : ℕ, 1 - ε ≤ (TwoPowAddSet r).lowerDensity` and updated the docstring to specify lower density. Also corrected the trivial citation error from “D. Price” to “L. Price.” Only 851.lean was edited. The required compile command succeeds with no warnings other than the two existing `sorry` warnings.
